items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Many of his recording feature the legendary trio with Ray Brown and Barney Kessel

ctx.x: From his recording debut at age 19, Canadian pianist Oscar Peterson has built a career that is unrivaled in the history of jazz. Mr. Peterson’s astounding technique and melodic inventiveness have placed him at the forefront of modern jazz pianists. Many of his recording feature the legendary trio with Ray Brown and Barney Kessel (later Herb Ellis and Ed Thigpen). His frequent visits to the recording studio have also yielded wonderful pairings with artists such as Count Basie, Dizzy Gillespie, Louis Armstrong and…

I am pleased indeed to be seated at the foot of the king — at the feet of the one and only Mr. Oscar Peterson. He has no idea how I feel about him, really, because I kid him, pretend that we are equals, but he’s the king, really. He is the king. Oscar, this thing that we are doing, we are trying to preserve for the younger generation, some of the history of our music — how we were inspired, who inspired us, and all of that.
